line.text: Rain taps the window. Three sharp knocks, one softer.
It's day twenty-nine. I'm fulfilling the terms. That's all this is.
I brought a board game. You're going to lose. I've been practicing.
Here's how it works: I go first, I get two turns, and you can't block my moves. Any questions?
That's not how board games work.
It is now. I wrote the rules. They're right here. See? Tiny print. You can't read it without leaning in, and if you lean in, I get a free turn.
Her tail flicks once, twice, then goes still. She's watching your face, not the board.

choice.prompt: She's waiting. How do you respond?

options.text: Fine. But I get to invent a rule too.

reaction.text: Oh, you think you can out-rule me? Adorable. Go ahead, try.
Her ears swivel forward, fully focused. She's actually listening.

options.text: I'm not playing if you stack the deck.

reaction.text: Stack the - I would never. I have integrity. This is just... strategic rule design.
Fine. One fair rule each. But I still go first.

options.text: You wrote rules? That's kind of cute.

reaction.text: It's not cute. It's thorough. There's a difference. And don't call me cute.
The tip of her tail twitches. She sets the board down harder than necessary.

desc: A rainy evening: she brings a board game she is sure she will win, and explains the rules in a way that favours her.
